report.verdict: Headline growth flattered (Net Revenue +19% to €1,220m / ~$1,338m) but the quality underwhelmed: comparable revenue +4%, comparable Adj. EBITDA +2%, Adj. EBITDA €396m (~$434m) roughly 10% below the Eurobank Equities estimate, margin down 410bps to 32.5%, and the explicit 37% FY26 margin guide quietly replaced by "within the consensus range" (€1,769–1,891m / ~$1.94–2.07bn). PrizePicks (+29% cFX revenue, +26% EBITDA on a 100% basis) and the UK's contractual cost recovery are the genuine positives; Betano's Brazil shutdown from 25 Sept, 3.5x leverage against a €1/share (~$1.10) distribution floor, and still-shrinking UK ticket sales are the overhangs. The shares' modest +1.6% on the day reflected a stock already down ~20% into the print, not relief in the numbers.

summary: **Headline beat on revenue, miss on profit.** Net Revenue €1,220m (~$1,338m), +19% YoY reported and marginally ahead of Eurobank Equities' €1,203m (Investing.com consensus €1.23bn); Adj. EBITDA €396m (~$434m), +6% YoY, c.10% below Eurobank's €440m, and Operating EBITDA €341m (~$374m) c.13% below Eurobank's €390m and c.20% below Citi. Adj. EPS €0.18 (~$0.20) vs €0.245 consensus.

**Strip out M&A and the quarter was +4%/+2%.** On the company's comparable basis (PrizePicks in the prior year; LottoItalia amortisation adjusted), Net Revenue +4% and Adj. EBITDA +2%. PrizePicks accounts for €183m of the €197m YoY revenue increase (93%); organic growth outside it was +€14m on a €1.0bn base.

**Margin −410bps to 32.5%: ~half mix, ~half operating.** Consolidating PrizePicks (17.8% margin) is structural dilution; the rest is the LottoItalia amortisation step-up (−€9m/qtr), Continental Europe marketing +21%, corporate costs +€6m, exceptionally customer-friendly sports results in Aug/Sep and a Q3-25 comp that management concedes was one of its highest-margin quarters in years. CFO called aggregate margin comparison 'a little bit misleading'.

**EBITDA guidance effectively softened, by Betano and sports results, not North America.** Q1 and Q2 guided FY26 Net Revenue growth 'mid-to-high 20%s' (before c.€60m / ~$66m one-offs) AND a 37% Adj. EBITDA margin. Q3 keeps the revenue guide but replaces 37% with 'within the range of consensus' (€1,769–1,891m / ~$1,941–2,074m, compiled 13 Nov). 37% on ~€5.1–5.2bn implied ~€1.89–1.92bn, i.e. the new range tops out where the old guide started. The drivers are Betano (Brazil shut from 25 Sept; share of net income flat at €35m vs €61m in Q2), customer-friendly sports outcomes (now including October) and lottery comps; North America was the one division running ahead.

**Implied Q4 is a wide corridor.** 9M-26 Adj. EBITDA €1,297m (~$1,423m, 35.3% margin) leaves €472–594m (~$518–652m) for Q4 vs €497m in Q4-25 (Allwyn International basis) or ~€572m pro forma including PrizePicks (our estimate). Citi expects the low end; we model ~€1.80–1.84bn (35–36% FY margin) — see Forecast.

**Product mix: iGaming and DFS carried the quarter, lottery and sports did not.** iGaming +26% to €151m (~$166m); DFS (PrizePicks, incl. prediction markets) €183m (~$201m), +24% reported/+29% cFX on a 100% basis; lottery −7% to €513m (~$563m) on record Tzoker/EuroMillions jackpots in Q3-25; sports betting +1% to €130m (~$143m) as higher stakes were offset by lower win margins (strong July incl. World Cup final stages, weak August/September); VLTs & casinos +2% to €142m.

**Digital now 47% of NGR.** Online NGR €530m (~$581m), +55% reported / +8% comparable, 47% of NGR (37% LY; 45% LY comparable) and 54% of online-eligible NGR. Continental Europe online +8% to €226m (32% share); Eurojackpot online (Greece, Aug) reached one in three online players in month one; UK online −9% to €121m.

**World Cup/NFL calendar: a modest net positive, then given back.** July benefited from the FIFA World Cup 2026 latter stages (good sports margins; PrizePicks had 25m+ World Cup line-ups across June/July per the Q2 release) but PrizePicks' July uplift was offset by the later NFL start, and group sports margins turned sharply customer-friendly in Aug/Sep. No group-level World Cup handle/actives are disclosed — a disclosure gap versus listed sportsbook peers.

**Operating EBITDA +13% as adjustments fall away.** EBITDA adjustments €55m (~$60m) vs €73m LY and the Q1 peak of €107m; UK transition costs now nil (vs €14m), PrizePicks transaction/retention €9m, IWG acquisition accounting €3m. The residual is dominated by the Allwyn global brand initiative (€30m in Q3, €32m corporate adjustments) — a recurring 'one-off' investors should treat as cost.

**UK cost-recovery, not UK growth.** UK Net Revenue −6% cFX to €237m (~$260m) with GGR −11% cFX to €883m (~$969m), yet Adj. EBITDA doubled to €18m (~$20m) because recovery of a portion of the ~£450m transformation spend started in Q2 under the licence's economic model. CAPEX fell to €10m from €38m; Powerball (July, first launch outside the US) has 1.3m+ players; a new leadership team is being installed.

**Cost/transformation programmes quantified.** UK: ~£450m transformation complete in Q1-26, CAPEX normalised (group CAPEX €51m, 4.2% of Net Revenue vs 7%); 'substantial majority' of transition costs recoverable over the 10-year licence. Kambi: €50m (~$55m) over 2027–29 to in-source sportsbook technology (capitalised; ~half in 2027) plus 'low tens of millions' of annual opex from 2027, offset by third-party supplier savings. Austria: €40m (~$44m) licence fee payable on award, tender expected 2027 (licence extended to end-2028).

**Cash flow weak in the quarter, leverage flat at 3.5x.** FCF €84m (~$92m) vs €215m: working-capital inflow €45m vs €152m, net finance costs paid €138m vs €70m (coupon timing), tax paid €102m. Net debt incl. leases €6,641m (~$7,285m), −€18m QoQ, 3.5x LTM PF Adj. EBITDA of €1,876m; cash €1,941m (~$2,129m) plus €936m (~$1,027m) undrawn facilities and €215m of Austrian money-market investments. CFO: 'above our leverage target' but 'no scenario' of covenant issues; 2026 is 'not a representative year' for cash flow.

**Capital returns delivered, but ahead of cash generation.** €150m (~$165m) buyback completed 5 Oct (11.34m shares, avg ~€13.23 — well above the current ~€9.7 price); €0.20 (~$0.22) interim paid 12 Nov with 2% of shares taking scrip; total 2026 distributions €1.00/share (~$1.10) and total returns €1.19/share (~$1.31). A €1/share floor on ~762m shares (~€762m p.a.) exceeds 9M FCF of €609m; management reiterated the floor holds 'even if Brazil remains shut'.

**Betano: growth decelerating, Brazil the swing factor.** 100% revenue +17% cFX to €795m (~$872m) (Q1 +31%, Q2 +26%); Operating EBITDA no longer disclosed (Q2: €257m). Brazil's regulated online market was closed by provisional measure on 25 Sept 2026; Betano is preparing mitigation for scenarios where some or all operations do not resume and targets 4 (release) to 5 (call) new countries in early 2027, Spain confirmed. 2026 dividends €701m (~$769m), +40%; Allwyn's ~36.75% share ~€258m (~$283m), including €55m from a €150m post-quarter payment.

**M&A/portfolio: small, bolt-on, capability-led.** Australian casinos sold (A$103m / €63m, €3m gain); Next Lotto (Germany) to 64.53% for ~€10m, consolidated from Q4; remaining 30% of IWG bought for USD122m (€107m), payable Q1-27; Brussels casino concession lost from July 2027 (<1% of CE EBITDA). Kambi deal keeps US sportsbook optionality open alongside PrizePicks.

**Governance and reporting basis.** Petra Ehmann proposed as INED, taking independents to 50% of the Board per the OPAP-combination commitment; KKCG holds 79.28%, free float 20.72%. IFRS comparatives are OPAP-only and 'differ materially'; all growth rates quoted are non-IFRS look-through. PPA for the OPAP combination is still open (Q3 PPA amortisation €82m; CFO: assume the run-rate persists and exclude from normalised EPS). IFRS profit for the period €37m (~$41m), attributable €22m.

**Sell-side response: estimates and targets cut, not raised.** Citi (Neutral, €10.40) sees FY26 Adj. EBITDA near the bottom of the consensus range and had cut its target from €11.70 in October; Eurobank Equities (Hold) held €11.10 on the day, then cut to €9.00 on 25 Nov, trimming PrizePicks EBITDA estimates ~10% for 2026 and 20–25% for 2027–28 and flagging dividend sustainability versus cash flow.

**Thesis read-through.** The diversification argument held in Q3 (one weak lever offset elsewhere) but the equity story now rests on (1) PrizePicks sustaining 20%+ growth through Q4/NFL-NBA and Packs, (2) a Brazil resolution or demonstrable Betano mitigation, and (3) deleveraging from 3.5x while paying €1/share. Q4 — the seasonally largest lottery quarter — must deliver ≥€472m of Adj. EBITDA just to reach the bottom of the range management has endorsed.

segments.name: Continental Europe (Austria, Czech Republic, Greece & Cyprus, Italy 32.5%, Germany, Slovakia)
segments.headline: Revenue +3% on a record-jackpot comp; Adj. EBITDA −3% (flat ex-LottoItalia amortisation) as marketing outran a flat NGR line.
narrative: They delivered Net Revenue of €754m (~$827m), +3% YoY and +3% QoQ, against a comparative in which GGR had grown 10%. GGR rose 1% to €1,161m (~$1,274m) with gaming taxes and good-cause contributions up 2% to €462m, so the net line was helped by non-gaming revenue (+38% to €55m). Austria led with +10%, the Czech Republic grew 4% and Greece & Cyprus were broadly stable — the latter carrying both the Tzoker jackpot comp (record high in August 2025) and the brunt of the customer-friendly sports results given OPAP's large sportsbook. By product, iGaming was again the engine (+26% to €151m / ~$166m), sports betting was +1% to €130m (~$143m) with higher amounts staked offset by lower win margins, lottery fell 8% to €276m (~$303m) and VLTs & casinos edged up 2% to €142m (~$156m). Sequentially, lottery rose 5% and sports betting fell 10% from the World Cup-boosted Q2. Note what is not disclosed: no sportsbook handle, net or structural win margin, promotional intensity, actives or ARPU are given for any market, so the volume/price/luck split rests on management's directional commentary.

Digital remained the growth lever: online NGR grew 8% to €226m (~$248m), lifting the online share of NGR to 32% from 30% and the share of online-eligible NGR to 41% from 38%. Eurojackpot online launched in Greece in August and reached one in three online players in its first month, and Greece's first Eurojackpot jackpot winner (€38m) was drawn the week of results; they also upgraded Keno in the Czech Republic and ran a gold-payout scratchcard in Austria. Nine-month online NGR is €715m (~$784m), +15%, with the online share at 34% versus 31% — a steady, not spectacular, mix shift for a lottery-led estate.

Adjusted EBITDA fell 3% to €328m (~$360m) for a 43.5% margin, −270bps YoY but +340bps QoQ from Q2's 40.1%. The entire YoY decline is the LottoItalia licence-fee amortisation step-up following the 30 Nov 2025 renewal: share of profit of equity-method investees fell to €8m from €19m (a €9m amortisation effect), and excluding it EBITDA was flat. Beneath that, the cost lines were less reassuring: marketing rose 21% to €80m, or 10.6% of Net Revenue versus 9.1% (9M: €255m, 11.4% vs 10.1%), agents' commissions and services rose 3% to €305m, and personnel fell 2% to €121m — i.e. operating costs grew faster than a +1% NGR. Management reminded that Q3-25 was one of the highest-margin quarters in years, which is true, but it also means the 9M margin of 42.3% (vs 44.5%) is the better guide to run-rate profitability. CAPEX was €15m (−17%) and Adj. EBITDA − CAPEX €313m (~$343m).

Portfolio and regulatory housekeeping was active. The non-core Australian casinos were sold in August for A$103m (€63m / ~$69m, €3m gain); the Next Lotto (Germany) stake rose to 46.29% in September and to a controlling 64.53% in October for ~€10m, with consolidation from Q4; the Brussels casino concession was awarded to another operator from July 2027 (under 1% of segment EBITDA in 2025). On licences, the Austrian exclusive lottery licence has been extended from September 2027 to end-2028 with a tender expected in 2027, a €40m (~$44m) fee on award and a 15-year term, and they will bid in coordination with state partner ÖBAG; the Greek legacy games licence runs to 2030. The Austrian gaming-tax increase annualised in Q2, so it is no longer a drag, while the c.€60m (~$66m) of 2026 one-off revenue impacts embedded in guidance sit in this segment.

segments.name: North America (PrizePicks, Allwyn LS Group incl. Illinois Lottery PMA, IWG) — 100% basis
segments.headline: PrizePicks re-accelerated to +29% cFX with customer activity +30%+ and EBITDA +26%, but the H1 wobble and a 17.8% Q3 margin keep the valuation debate open.
narrative: Presented as if PrizePicks had been owned in both periods, they grew North America Net Revenue 21% in constant currency (20% reported) to €242m (~$265m); on a reported basis the comparative is just €55m because PrizePicks was consolidated from 16 January 2026. PrizePicks itself grew Net Revenue 29% cFX (24% reported) to €183m (~$201m), with customer activity — DFS entry fees plus the real cash customers commit to prediction-market contracts, explicitly not notional contract value — up more than 30% YoY across both DFS and prediction markets. There was no material sports-outcome effect this quarter; the World Cup helped July but was offset by the later NFL start. Non-gaming revenue (Illinois management fee and operating allowance, IWG and Allwyn Lottery Solutions technology sales) grew 7% to €59m. Sequentially Net Revenue fell 18% from Q2's €294m, the usual summer trough. Context matters for the re-acceleration: on the same 100% basis PrizePicks revenue was €236m vs €239m in Q1 and €231m vs €235m in Q2, held back by operator-friendly outcomes in the comparatives, so part of Q3's +29% is normalisation rather than a new gear; 9M segment revenue is up only 5% on a 100% basis.

Engagement indicators were uniformly positive but almost entirely qualitative. They describe PrizePicks as the clear DFS market leader on 24-month app downloads, say monthly actives grew sequentially from the August low and accelerated into the NFL, NHL and NBA season starts, that October saw record customer activity and that November month-to-date MAUs are up by a double-digit percentage YoY (the Q2 release had June paying MAUs +18%). Product cadence was high: fully blended line-ups combining player, team and culture picks ahead of the NFL, and in October the launch of Packs — collectible trading-card packs opened in-app with genuine ownership of graded, physically deliverable cards, grail cards valued up to $8m, and a ~$3m Dylan Harper rookie card pulled from a $25 pack. Management says the majority of loyal DFS customers have already bought Packs, that it is reactivating dormant players and bringing in a new audience, and that it is year-round and independent of sports outcomes; PrizePicks acts as a broker in prediction markets, earning commission without outcome risk. What is still missing are absolute MAUs, ARPU, the DFS versus prediction-market revenue split and any hold-rate disclosure, so the 'ecosystem' thesis cannot yet be stress-tested from the outside.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 26% to €43m (~$47m) for a 17.8% margin, +100bps YoY but −1,760bps QoQ (35.4% in Q2, 33.0% in Q1): the Q3 margin is depressed by seasonally low revenue against a marketing line that was flat QoQ at €75m (~$82m), +14% YoY, equal to 31.0% of Net Revenue (32.7% LY; 25.5% in Q2 when World Cup acquisition spend was described as €25m above the prior year). Materials and services were €74m (+12%), personnel €65m (−2%), and EBITDA adjustments fell to €13m from €29m (transaction and retention costs €9m, IWG earn-out/put accounting €3m); the CFO cautioned that Q1–Q2 unadjusted cost lines were inflated by acquisition-related items. On a 100% basis 9M Adj. EBITDA is €245m, −12% YoY, which is the number the bears will cite; the Illinois fee structure is largely cost pass-through, diluting margin but not EBITDA. CAPEX was €13m (+44%). Marketing will, they say, be flexed on CAC and payback, with Packs expected to lift retention and reduce acquisition spend over time.

Strategically, the quarter tightened ownership of capabilities: the remaining 30% of IWG was bought in October after a put exercise for USD122m (€107m / ~$117m), payable in Q1-27, and the Kambi agreement gives a US-proven sportsbook stack that management explicitly keeps available for a potential US sportsbook alongside PrizePicks. The Illinois PMA three-year extension legislation had passed both chambers as of Q1 with commercial terms outstanding; there was no update in the Q3 release. Q4 is PrizePicks' largest quarter and will carry Packs' first full period; Eurobank Equities nonetheless cut its PrizePicks EBITDA estimates by ~10% for 2026 and 20–25% for 2027–28 after the print. The unaddressed risk is regulatory — DFS pick'em and sports-event prediction markets remain contested at state and federal level and the release is silent on it.

segments.name: United Kingdom (Allwyn UK — The National Lottery, fourth licence from Feb 2024)
segments.headline: Ticket sales still falling (GGR −11% cFX) but Adj. EBITDA doubled on contractual recovery of the ~£450m transformation spend; profit is a mechanism, not momentum.
narrative: They reported UK Net Revenue of €237m (~$260m), −6% in constant currency and −5% reported, flat QoQ, while GGR — the number that actually measures player demand — fell 11% cFX (−9% reported) to €883m (~$969m). The explanations were a strong comparative with favourable EuroMillions jackpot cycles and players continuing to adjust to the new website and app introduced in Q1, partly offset by Powerball, launched in July as the first deployment of the game outside the United States and already with more than 1.3m players. The sequence is the problem: GGR has now fallen YoY in Q1 (−4% cFX), Q2 (−14% cFX) and Q3 (−11% cFX), and online NGR fell 9% to €121m (~$133m), taking the online share to 51% from 53% — the digital channel that the £450m transformation was built to grow is where the erosion is concentrated. Other product initiatives included the enhanced Lotto format (June), £10 instant-win games, a £10 scratchcard pilot from September, and more than 1,700 third-party quick-commerce stores now selling scratchcards.

The economics explain why profit rose as sales fell. Under the fourth licence's model, Allwyn began in Q2 to recover a portion of the approximately £450m invested in the technology transformation, so gaming taxes and good-cause contributions fell 11% to €646m (73.2% of GGR vs 74.3%) and agents' commissions, materials and services fell 21% to €119m. Adj. EBITDA doubled to €18m (~$20m) for a 7.6% margin (+400bps YoY; 9.7% in Q2), marketing was flat at €62m (26.2% of Net Revenue vs 24.8%), personnel fell 10% to €38m, and transition-cost adjustments were nil against €14m a year ago. CAPEX fell to €10m from €38m (and from €13m in Q2), so Adj. EBITDA − CAPEX swung to +€8m from −€29m. Nine-month UK Adj. EBITDA is €45m (~$49m) vs €24m on flat Net Revenue of €697m (~$765m), with CAPEX of €41m vs €107m; the 'substantial majority' of transition costs is expected to be recoverable over the 10-year licence.

Management's framing was 'restoring momentum' and 'progressively restore sustainable growth', and they confirmed a new leadership team is being installed to lead the next stage of the transformation 'especially in digital'. Our read is that the cash-flow turn is real and largely contractual, which makes it dependable but also finite, whereas the operating recovery is unproven: returns to Good Causes are lower YoY, and a lottery monopoly losing double-digit GGR for three quarters is a regulatory as well as a commercial sensitivity. Q4 is the seasonally strongest lottery quarter and the EuroMillions/Powerball jackpot cycle is the main swing factor into year-end; we would want to see GGR declines narrow to low single digits and online NGR return to growth before crediting the UK with anything beyond cost recovery.

blocks.takeaway: UK Net Revenue €237m (~$260m), −6% cFX, while GGR fell 11% cFX (−9% reported) to €883m (~$969m).
points: Explanations: strong comparative with favourable EuroMillions jackpot cycles, and players adjusting to the new website and app from Q1.

segments.name: Betano (Kaizen Gaming) — ~36.75% equity-accounted; 100% basis unless stated
segments.headline: Revenue +17% cFX but decelerating; share of net income flat at €35m and EBITDA disclosure dropped; Brazil closed from 25 Sept is the 2027 swing factor.
narrative: Betano grew total revenue 17% in constant currency (21% reported) to €795m (~$872m), a clear deceleration from +31% cFX in Q1 (€788m) and +26% in Q2 (€972m); sequentially revenue fell 18%. Sports margins were exceptionally customer-friendly in both Q3-26 and Q3-25 and broadly similar, and the final days of the quarter carried the first impact of the closure of Brazil's regulated online sports betting and iGaming market after a provisional measure entered into force on 25 September 2026. Allwyn's share of net income rose 3% to €35m (~$38m), but that is 43% below Q2's €61m, and the release no longer shows Betano's Operating EBITDA (Q2: €257m, +24%) — the CFO declined to add anything beyond the statement, which we read as a step back in transparency at precisely the wrong moment. Nine-month revenue is €2,555m (~$2,803m), +25%, and Allwyn's 9M equity income €156m (~$171m), 12% of group Adj. EBITDA.

Cash is the more important channel for Allwyn. No dividend was received in Q3, but Betano paid €150m (~$165m) after the quarter — i.e. after the Brazilian measure — of which Allwyn's share is ~€55m (~$60m); 2026 dividends total €701m (~$769m), +40% on €501m, with Allwyn's share ~€258m (~$283m) vs €184m. Betano is net cash with no debt and, per management, has 'many levers to optimize cash flow', underpinning the commitment that it will pay 'material dividends in 2027 in any scenario'. Brazil was the largest market in Q3 but the rest of a 20-plus-country footprint contributes the majority of revenue; four new countries are targeted for early 2027 per the release (five per the call, Spain confirmed), which would take the footprint to 24. Chile's regulatory initiatives are being monitored with scenario plans; Betano's country revenue split is not disclosed.

Our read: Eurobank Equities already removes Brazil from its Betano valuation and estimates the suspension costs Allwyn c.3% of consolidated Adj. EBITDA and 5–6% of adjusted net profit in both 2026 and 2027; that looks light if Brazil stays shut all year given it was the largest market, but Betano's historical speed to scale and profitability in new markets is a genuine offset. The Kambi decision — in-sourcing sportsbook technology rather than leaning on Betano's platform — confirms Allwyn is building its own sportsbook capability independent of the associate, and keeps US sportsbook optionality separate from Betano's roadmap. For 2027, the Betano dividend is the single biggest determinant of whether the €1/share (~$1.10) distribution is funded from cash flow or from the balance sheet.

highlights.text: PrizePicks re-accelerated: Net Revenue +29% cFX (+24% reported) to €183m (~$201m) with customer activity >+30% YoY across DFS and prediction markets, Adj. EBITDA +26% to €43m (~$47m) on a 100% basis, record customer activity in October and Nov MTD MAUs +double-digit % YoY; Packs adds a year-round, outcome-independent vertical.

iGaming +26% to €151m (~$166m) and online NGR +8% comparable (47% of group NGR; Continental Europe 32%, +2pp): the digital mix shift continues through a weak lottery/sports quarter, and Eurojackpot online reached one in three Greek online players in its first month.

UK cash flow has turned: Adj. EBITDA doubled to €18m (~$20m), CAPEX fell to €10m from €38m, transition-cost adjustments to nil from €14m, and Adj. EBITDA − CAPEX swung to +€8m from −€29m as recovery of the ~£450m transformation spend runs under the licence; group CAPEX is now 4.2% of Net Revenue vs 7%.

Operating EBITDA (pre add-backs) +13% to €341m (~$374m) with adjustments halved from the Q1 peak to €55m (~$60m); Adj. EBITDA − CAPEX +14% to €345m (~$378m) — the quality-of-earnings gap between operating and adjusted is narrowing as promised.

Capital returns delivered on schedule: €150m (~$165m) buyback completed, €0.20 (~$0.22) interim paid, €1.00/share (~$1.10) distributions and €1.19/share (~$1.31) total returns in 2026; the €1/share floor was reiterated 'even if Brazil remains shut', and no material debt maturities fall before 2029.

Betano cash remains strong despite Brazil: €150m (~$165m) dividend paid after the provisional measure, 2026 dividends €701m (~$769m) +40%, Allwyn's share ~€258m (~$283m); net cash, no debt, 4–5 new markets in early 2027 (Spain confirmed).

Capability in-sourcing at modest cost: Kambi perpetual source-code licence for €50m (~$55m) over 2027–29 (capitalised) with offsetting third-party supplier savings; full ownership of IWG (USD122m / €107m); Next Lotto consolidated from Q4 — all bolt-on, none balance-sheet-stretching.

lowlights.text: The 37% FY26 Adj. EBITDA margin guide from Q1/Q2 was replaced by 'within the consensus range' (€1,769–1,891m / ~$1,941–2,074m) without being called a cut; 37% on guided revenue implied ~€1.89–1.92bn (est.), i.e. the top of the new range. 9M margin is 35.3% and Q3 32.5% (−410bps YoY). Citi expects the low end.

Betano's Brazil market closed on 25 Sept 2026 by provisional measure, with no reopening timetable; Betano revenue growth has decelerated from +31% to +17% cFX across 2026, share of net income fell to €35m (~$38m) from €61m QoQ, and Betano's Operating EBITDA is no longer disclosed.

Q3 profit missed the sell side: Adj. EBITDA €396m (~$434m) ~10% below Eurobank Equities' €440m; Operating EBITDA €341m ~13% below Eurobank and ~20% below Citi; Adj. EPS €0.18 (~$0.20) vs €0.245 consensus. Comparable growth of +4% revenue / +2% EBITDA is well below the high-single-digit medium-term ambition flagged by Barclays on the call.

Leverage 3.5x (net debt incl. leases €6,641m / ~$7,285m), above the company's own target, while the €1/share floor (~€762m p.a.) exceeds 9M FCF of €609m (~$668m); Q3 FCF was only €84m (~$92m) as net finance costs paid rose to €138m and working-capital inflow shrank to €45m from €152m. Sofokleous10/Eurobank flag the dividend as cash-flow-uncovered in 2026 (management: 'not a representative year').

UK demand is still shrinking: GGR −11% cFX (third consecutive quarterly decline), online NGR −9% with the online share down to 51%, and Good Cause returns lower; the EBITDA improvement is a contractual cost-recovery mechanism, not operating leverage, and a new leadership team is only now being installed.

Cost creep beneath the surface: Continental Europe marketing +21% (10.6% of NR vs 9.1%) on +1% NGR; corporate costs +€6m with eliminations 'creeping up'; the Allwyn brand initiative (€30m in Q3, recurring since 2025) is still treated as an EBITDA add-back; Kambi adds 'low tens of millions' of annual opex from 2027.

Sports-outcome and jackpot luck were both adverse: group sports betting +1% and lottery −7% on Tzoker/EuroMillions record-jackpot comps, with exceptionally customer-friendly results in Aug/Sep and, per the CFO, October too — already baked into Q4 guidance, which is why the implied Q4 corridor is so wide.

forecast.intro: Old versus new: at Q1 (4 June) and Q2 (27 Aug) Allwyn guided FY26 consolidated Net Revenue growth of 'mid-to-high 20%s' before c.€60m (~$66m, c.−2%) of one-off Continental Europe impacts AND an Adj. EBITDA margin of 37%. At Q3 the revenue guide is reaffirmed but the margin guide is gone, replaced by 'Adj. EBITDA within the range of consensus expectations' — a company-compiled €1,769–1,891m (~$1,941–2,074m) as of 13 Nov — and management confirmed the outlook already factors in customer-friendly October sports results. Arithmetically, 37% on an FY26 revenue base of ~€5.1–5.2bn (FY25 €4,112m grown 24–27%) implied ~€1.89–1.92bn, so the new range tops out roughly where the old guide began; at the €1,830m midpoint the effective change is c.−€60–90m (our estimate). The divisions driving the softening are Betano (Brazil closure from 25 Sept, flat equity income) and Continental Europe (LottoItalia amortisation −€9m/qtr, sports margins, marketing +21%), with the UK neutral-to-positive on cost recovery and North America (PrizePicks EBITDA +26%) the only division running ahead. With 9M Adj. EBITDA at €1,297m (~$1,423m), the implied Q4 is €472–594m (~$518–652m) against €497m in Q4-25 on the Allwyn International basis (~€572m pro forma including ~€75m of PrizePicks, our estimate from the disclosed €83m for 1 Oct 25–15 Jan 26).

forecast.view: **Revenue:** we model Q4-26 Net Revenue of ~€1.44bn (~$1.58bn) — Q4-25 €1,120m plus ~€300–320m of PrizePicks in its seasonally largest quarter (+25% on an estimated ~€250m Q4-25 base, with Packs' first full quarter), Continental Europe +3% and the UK −5% — giving FY26 ~€5.1bn (~$5.6bn), +24% reported or ~+26% before the €60m one-offs: inside the guided range but at its low end, and sensitive to Q4 jackpot cycles (EuroMillions/Powerball/Eurojackpot) and October's sports results. **Margin/EBITDA:** we estimate Q4 Adj. EBITDA of ~€505–545m (~$554–598m): ~€572m pro forma base, less ~€9m LottoItalia amortisation, ~€20–30m lower Betano equity income if Brazil stays shut for the quarter, ~€10m of adverse October sports margins and higher corporate/marketing run-rate, partly offset by ~€15–20m of PrizePicks growth and UK cost recovery. That gives FY26 ~€1.80–1.84bn (~$1.98–2.02bn), a 35–36% margin — lower-to-mid of the consensus range and ~€50–100m below the old 37% guide; we would not model the top of the range. **Leverage:** Q4 is seasonally cash-generative and brings ~€55m from Betano, but the €149m cash interim was paid in November and USD122m for IWG, ~€25m of Kambi capex, the €40m Austrian licence fee and ~€762m of 2027 distributions all sit ahead; we see YE26 net debt/EBITDA of ~3.3–3.5x and a glide path to ~3.0x only by end-2027, and only if Betano's 2027 dividend is at least maintained. **Swing factors:** Brazil (reopening vs. prolonged closure is a ~€100m+ swing in 2027 equity income and dividends, our estimate), PrizePicks Q4 hold and Packs economics, UK digital GGR stabilisation, Austrian licence award and the still-open OPAP PPA (D&A run-rate). On these numbers the equity is being asked to underwrite a 2027 dividend from a balance sheet rather than from demonstrated cash flow, which is why we expect the shares to trade on Brazil headlines and PrizePicks data points rather than on Q4 lottery seasonality.
watch: Brazil: any reversal, judicial challenge or re-regulation of the 25 Sept provisional measure, Betano's mitigation actions and the size/timing of its 2027 dividends (2026: €701m / ~$769m total, ~€258m / ~$283m to Allwyn).

PrizePicks Q4: NFL/NBA season activity, MAU growth (Nov MTD +double-digit %), Packs attach and reactivation metrics, marketing % of revenue (31% in Q3) and any state or federal regulatory action on DFS pick'em / sports prediction markets.

Q4 Adj. EBITDA versus the €472m floor implied by the bottom of the consensus range; FY26 margin versus the withdrawn 37% guide; whether 2027 guidance (due with FY results, ~March 2027) restores an explicit margin framework.

UK: GGR trend (−11% cFX in Q3) and online NGR (−9%) under the incoming leadership team; Powerball/EuroMillions jackpot cycles; Good Cause contributions and any Gambling Commission scrutiny of the sales decline.

Balance sheet: YE26 net debt/EBITDA (3.5x at Q3) versus the €1/share (~$1.10) floor, USD122m IWG payment in Q1-27, ~€25m Kambi capex in 2027, €40m (~$44m) Austrian licence fee on award; finalisation of the OPAP PPA and the IFRS 9M statements (published 26 Nov).

Continental Europe cost discipline: marketing (10.6% of NR, +150bps YoY) and corporate costs (+€6m) against ~flat NGR; Austrian lottery licence tender process in 2027; consolidation of Next Lotto from Q4.

Disclosure: restoration of Betano Operating EBITDA, and any first disclosure of PrizePicks MAUs/ARPU or OPAP sportsbook handle and margins — the absence of all of these is itself a risk flag for a Euronext Athens large-cap.
